gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the only approved store selling a golf-cart audio part, Vatrer, sells its 25 A / 335 W 12 V reducer as two separate $79.99 models (36V, and 48V/72V), or that Vatrer asks for the reducer's base to sit against metal to shed heat under long, heavy load.
standout_why: I read golfcartbase.com (cited), cartvoltage.com and nicksgolfcarts.com on 2026-11-10. mtx.com (cited) returned HTTP 403. All three pages I read already cover the core rules: a 12 V reducer is required on 36/48 V carts, size it for the load (cartvoltage says at least 30 A, 40 A for big bars; Nick's says 10 A for a bar alone, 20 A with lights), fuse near the source, run the negative to the reducer or pack and not the frame, wire the reducer to the key switch, and check the reducer's input range against lithium charge voltage (cartvoltage gives 58.4 V). None of them names a reducer that can be bought with the speaker in one approved cart. None gives Vatrer's separate 36 V and 48 V/72 V SKUs or its instruction to bolt the base to metal. Nick's covers only part of the heat point ('dry, ventilated'). The fact is new but does not decide the set, and two rival pages give reducer sizing that disagrees (10–20 A vs 30 A+), so a 25 A unit falls between them.
kit_items: 12 V reducer: Vatrer 48V/72V to 12V 25A/335W (or the separate Vatrer 36V to 12V 25A model for 36 V carts). It is the only reducer in an approved store. 25 A covers a soundbar alone by Nick's 10 A rule and a bar plus LED lights by Nick's 20 A rule. It is below cartvoltage's 30 A minimum for a bar with lights.

Hardwired 12 V soundbar: bought on Amazon, because no approved non-Amazon store sells a golf-cart soundbar. cartvoltage names the ECOXGEAR SoundExtreme 18-inch (about $300, IP66) and the Wet Sounds Stealth 6 Ultra HD (about $400–480, IP67, 200 W RMS). The BOSS BRT26RGB that ChatGPT showed is marked discontinued at Sonic Electronix.
Inline fuse holder on the reducer's output: sized to the soundbar maker's spec. cartvoltage says 10–20 A is typical, fitted close to the reducer.
Key-switch relay or the reducer's enable lead: so the bar and reducer draw nothing while parked. Nick's puts Bluetooth amp idle draw at 0.25–2 A.
Wire and loom: negative run to the reducer or pack negative. Never tap 12 V from the middle of the battery string (Nick's).
